interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Derived algebraic geometry, large-cardinal research and exhaustive specialized geometric-analysis programs are beyond this representative progression.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Vendor credentials, chip fabrication and production-scale foundation-model infrastructure are excluded, not assumed prerequisites.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.domain: Chemical professional qualifications and additional specialties
exclusions.rationale: Radiation-handling licensure, industrial process credentials and exhaustive specialized synthesis families are excluded. Scientific isotope tracing is included at undergraduate core through chemistry/isotope-and-environmental-chemistry: isotope-tracers.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.domain: Additional physical frontiers and facility qualifications
exclusions.rationale: Quantum gravity, string theory, exhaustive particle-model extensions and specialized accelerator or fusion-facility operation are outside this progression.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.domain: Biological professional qualifications and additional specialties
exclusions.rationale: Clinical, veterinary and environmental credentials, exhaustive taxonomic catalogs and every frontier synthetic-biology platform are excluded; they are not prerequisites.

includes: Single-cell/multi-omics, sequence models and structural interpretation
excludes: Every omics platform and de novo folding algorithm

outcomes.description: Implement sequence HMM forward/backward inference; use documented protein-structure/interaction tools with coordinate/confidence interpretation and validate functional hypotheses against independent experiments and leakage-aware benchmarks.
Construct count and latent-variable models for bulk/single-cell data; account for batch/missingness and integrate expression, accessibility and sequence without equating clusters and cell identities.

practice: Reanalyze multi-omics data and implement a sequence model, separating computational confidence from experimental mechanism validation.

includes: Ethology, behavioral sampling, learning, communication and social evolution

outcomes.description: Compare proximate and evolutionary explanations of foraging, mating, cooperation and parental care using bounded payoff and inclusive-fitness models; assess anthropomorphism and welfare tradeoffs.
Construct operational ethograms, implement focal/scan sampling and estimate observer reliability; design controlled preference, learning and communication tests.

practice: Code blinded animal videos and test competing behavioral explanations with a sampling and welfare justification.

includes: Biological technique, assay controls and experimental design

outcomes.description: Perform dilution, sterile transfer, nonpathogenic culture, microscopy, DNA extraction, PCR and gels; explain assay representations, controls and failures.
Design replicated, randomized and blinded experiments; distinguish technical/biological replication and justify welfare, consent, biosafety and provenance decisions.

practice: Conduct supervised culture/PCR work with contamination checks, positive/negative controls and a prespecified analysis.

includes: Membranes, organelles, cytoskeleton, cell cycle, signaling and imaging

outcomes.description: Explain transport, compartmentation, trafficking, cytoskeletal movement, division and receptor signaling using molecular interactions and concentration gradients.
Interpret light/fluorescence images with scale bars, controls and resolution limits; quantify cell size, localization and division counts.

practice: Quantify microscopy images and distinguish altered localization, population size and imaging artifact.

includes: Quantitative imaging, signaling and causal cellular research

outcomes.description: Integrate timed perturbations, rescue, live imaging and molecular readouts to distinguish signaling, mechanical and fate mechanisms; justify organism choice and welfare/consent tradeoffs.
Use documented segmentation/tracking after learning thresholding, connected components and assignment procedures; quantify localization, trajectories and lineages with artifact/uncertainty checks.

practice: Audit live-cell image analysis and design a factorial perturbation study with quantified competing predictions.

includes: Conductance dynamics, neural circuits, point processes and coding

outcomes.description: Derive conditional-intensity likelihood from time bins, fit encoding/decoding models and calculate taught entropy/mutual-information measures with sampling bias and held-out checks.
Derive membrane/gating equations; implement conductance-based neurons and excitatory/inhibitory networks; analyze excitability, equilibria, oscillations and explicit plasticity rules.

practice: Implement a conductance circuit and fit spike encoding, comparing mechanistic, predictive and intervention evidence.

includes: Biodiversity threats, spatial assessment, restoration and decisions

outcomes.description: Assess extinction, fragmentation, invasion and climate pressures using abundance, occupancy and mapped habitats with detection and scale limitations.
Compare protection, restoration and harvest interventions using objectives, uncertainty, costs, Indigenous/local knowledge and stakeholder obligations.

practice: Use a provided GIS viewer and monitoring data to defend a reserve/restoration plan and adaptive decision protocol.

includes: Patterning, differentiation, morphogenesis and developmental inference

outcomes.description: Interpret lineage tracing, transplantation, mosaics and loss/gain-of-function evidence; distinguish autonomy, competence and instructive signaling using controlled tests.
Explain axes, induction, morphogen thresholds, fate specification and tissue movement using lineage and spatial-expression representations in animals and plants.

practice: Reconstruct a mechanism from spatial images and perturbations and propose a decisive rescue or lineage experiment.

includes: Eco-evolutionary feedback, spatial models and hierarchical field inference

outcomes.description: Derive invasion-fitness and coupled trait/population models; implement patch and individual-based stochastic models and compare deterministic, stochastic and scale-dependent predictions.
Construct hierarchical demographic/environmental/genetic models, evaluate posterior predictions and design monitoring or experiments distinguishing eco-evolutionary mechanisms.

practice: Fit an integrated population model and defend a feasible, ethically justified design separating competing spatial/evolutionary mechanisms.

includes: Population/community ecology, ecosystems, selection and macroevolution

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete growth, energy/nutrient budgets and diversity measures; estimate abundance from quadrats and mark-recapture data with explicit detection assumptions.
Compare selection, drift, gene flow, speciation and historical explanations using traits, fossils and environments; separate ecological association from causation.

practice: Analyze field surveys and a trait-frequency time series, checking detection and alternative evolutionary explanations.

includes: Study designs, risk measures, causal bias and discrete transmission

outcomes.description: Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk and odds ratios; compare cohort, case-control and trial evidence with confounding, selection and measurement-bias diagrams.
Construct spreadsheet susceptible-infectious-recovered recurrences from contact/recovery probabilities; compare screening or prevention policies using uncertainty, privacy and equity.

practice: Evaluate screening and outbreak datasets and recommend a policy with explicit causal and distributional limitations.

includes: Selection, drift, migration, coalescence and phylogenetic inference

outcomes.description: Construct parsimony and sequence-likelihood trees using a taught finite-state substitution/pruning model; assess bootstrap support, homoplasy and model sensitivity.
Derive allele-frequency recurrences and implement Wright-Fisher sampling, mutation, migration and selection; calculate heterozygosity, linkage disequilibrium and simple coalescent probabilities.

practice: Implement population sampling and small-tree likelihood calculations and compare competing histories.

includes: Inheritance, meiosis, linkage and genetic evidence

outcomes.description: Use mutation, complementation and segregation evidence to infer gene relationships and environmental effects; evaluate genetic privacy and deterministic claims.
Predict pedigree and cross probabilities with linkage, sex linkage, epistasis and cytoplasmic inheritance; estimate recombination maps.

practice: Analyze blinded crosses and pedigrees and defend a genetic model and limits on individual prediction.

includes: Reads, alignment, assembly, variants and genomic testing

outcomes.description: Explain sequencing reads and quality scores; implement dynamic-programming alignment and small de Bruijn assembly; interpret repeats, coverage and mapping limits.
Build documented QC, variant and expression-count workflows; calculate genotype likelihoods under a taught read-error model and apply locally taught false-discovery control.

practice: Analyze public or synthetic reads, preserve provenance/privacy and verify calls against known simulated truth.

includes: Innate/adaptive immunity, tolerance, vaccination and assays

outcomes.description: Interpret ELISA, flow-cytometry gates and vaccination data using taught signal models, controls and denominators; distinguish correlates from demonstrated protection.
Trace recognition, presentation, activation, receptor diversification, effectors, memory and tolerance; explain allergy, autoimmunity and immune evasion.

practice: Construct control-aware gates and defend a limited vaccine-response claim from multigroup assay data.

includes: Host-microbe mechanisms, immune repertoires and causal research

outcomes.description: Construct testable models of invasion, microbial competition, immune evasion, tolerance and memory; interpret repertoire and single-cell assay evidence with explicit sampling/selection limits.
Design controlled perturbation, co-culture, neutralization and longitudinal immune studies; distinguish host and microbial mechanisms and justify welfare, biosafety, consent and translational limits.

practice: Analyze a curated host-microbe perturbation dataset and defend discriminating experiments using nonpathogenic surrogates or existing evidence.

includes: Cells, organisms, inheritance, evolution and biological evidence

outcomes.description: Distinguish observation from mechanism, compare evolutionary explanations and design controlled comparisons with measurable biological variables.
Diagram cellular organization, major biomolecule roles, energy and matter exchange, DNA inheritance and organism-environment relationships.

practice: Compare unfamiliar organisms and critique competing explanations for a controlled growth experiment.

includes: Microbial metabolism, replication, ecology and identification

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal, fungal and viral replication, metabolic strategies and gene exchange; calculate growth and viable counts from dilution data.
Combine culture, staining, biochemical, susceptibility and sequence-assay evidence; distinguish resistance, contamination, colonization and causal infection.

practice: Investigate a nonpathogenic isolate or curated case using orthogonal tests and contamination controls.

includes: Genome maintenance, expression, chromatin and intervention

outcomes.description: Trace replication, repair, recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and chromatin regulation; predict sequence/regulatory perturbation consequences.
Design cloning, reporters, qPCR, editing and rescue using construct maps, guide/primer constraints and controls; distinguish off-target, dosage and regulatory effects.

practice: Design and, where authorized, execute a benign reporter perturbation with sequence verification, normalization and rescue.

includes: Neural signals, circuits, plasticity and behavioral evidence

outcomes.description: Use taught Nernst, RC and threshold/reset models for bounded neuronal responses; explain active spikes, synapses and plasticity and passive-model limitations.
Relate sensory, motor, autonomic and memory circuits to anatomy/behavior; quantify spike histograms and receptive fields and evaluate recording, lesion and intervention evidence.

practice: Analyze neural/behavioral recordings and identify where passive membrane predictions require active-channel mechanisms.

includes: Major lineages, comparative anatomy, life cycles and adaptations

outcomes.description: Classify representative bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants and animals using diagnostic characters; construct a small character-based phylogenetic hypothesis.
Compare body plans, reproduction, nutrition and environmental adaptations while distinguishing homology, convergence and functional constraint.

practice: Build a comparative specimen portfolio and defend a character matrix and tree against alternative codings.

includes: Animal organ systems, plant transport, feedback and homeostasis

outcomes.description: Analyze cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine, muscular and reproductive function using explicitly taught mass-balance, pressure-flow, diffusion, receptor and feedback models.
Explain water potential, xylem/phloem, mineral nutrition, stomata, photosynthetic exchange and plant hormones; calculate bounded transport and water-balance predictions.

practice: Interpret animal-homeostasis and plant gas-exchange perturbations using compartment diagrams and mass balances.

includes: Plant development, stress physiology, symbiosis and research design
excludes: Agronomic licensure and unrestricted field release

outcomes.description: Connect hormonal/developmental networks, source-sink relations, photosynthetic regulation, nutrient symbioses and stress acclimation to measurable plant phenotypes and competing mechanisms.

Design factorial genotype-environment experiments using gas exchange, fluorescence, isotope/transport readouts and molecular perturbations with taught assay models; assess developmental timing, chamber effects and ecological release consequences.

practice: Analyze a genotype-by-environment experiment and design orthogonal physiological and molecular tests of a stress-response mechanism.

includes: Ecological dynamics, structured populations and process/observation models

outcomes.description: Analyze logistic, consumer-resource, competition and age/stage-matrix models; calculate equilibria, stability, growth and sensitivity.
Construct and fit dynamic abundance, occupancy and capture-recapture likelihoods with detection error; assess process/observation separation, identifiability and held-out prediction.

practice: Infer population trajectories with imperfect detection and compare competing dynamical models on held-out surveys.

includes: Experimental structural biology, inverse representations and interaction assays

outcomes.description: Design purification and binding/stability assays using taught chromatography, equilibrium occupancy, calorimetric and fluorescence response models; infer affinity, stoichiometry and conformational change with controls.

Relate reciprocal-space intensities, projection images and NMR restraints to three-dimensional coordinates using taught discrete Fourier sums and forward models; use documented crystallographic/cryo-EM/restraint tools and assess phases, resolution, overfitting and ensemble ambiguity.

practice: Reconstruct or refine a small supplied structural dataset with documented tools and challenge its model using withheld data and orthogonal binding evidence.

includes: Biomolecular ensembles, allostery, kinetic states and structural inverse inference
excludes: Every single-molecule instrument and folding algorithm

outcomes.description: Fit structural restraints and fluorescence/force/kinetic observations using explicit noise and state models; quantify degeneracy, model selection and predictive validation against held-out perturbations.
Derive partition-function models of folding, binding and allostery and finite-state kinetic transition models; connect microscopic states to bulk and single-molecule observables.

practice: Infer a conformational-state model from complementary structural and kinetic data and design a perturbation distinguishing equally good fits.

includes: Biochemical networks, flux, regulation and system identification

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action/enzyme ODEs for metabolism and regulation; analyze conservation, flux null spaces, feedback, bistability and oscillation.
Fit dynamic parameters with documented optimizers, implement sensitivity equations/profile likelihoods and design perturbations distinguishing structural and practical nonidentifiability.

practice: Implement and fit a regulatory ODE model and design a measurement resolving demonstrated parameter ambiguity.

includes: Advanced separations, tandem detection, chemometrics and method validation

outcomes.description: Construct multivariate calibration and designed method-optimization experiments; assess traceability, selectivity, limits, recovery, drift and interlaboratory uncertainty using independent validation data.

Derive plate/retention and van-Deemter models with stated transport assumptions; design LC/GC/electrophoretic separations and tandem-MS acquisition and distinguish coelution, fragmentation and matrix suppression.

practice: Develop a mixture-analysis method and challenge it with blinded matrix, concentration and instrument-shift samples.

includes: Spin dynamics, multidimensional NMR and time-resolved molecular spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Develop density-operator spin notation, rotating frames and pulse propagators; derive two-spin echo/COSY/HSQC pathways, simulate finite Fourier acquisition and analyze relaxation and artifacts.

Model pump-probe, fluorescence and exchange signals using coupled kinetic equations and instrument-response convolution; fit global spectra/time courses and assess resolution, identifiability and competing mechanisms.

practice: Implement a two-spin pulse experiment and compare kinetic hypotheses against response-convolved time-resolved spectra.

includes: Stereoselective synthesis, pericyclic/catalytic transformations and route validation

outcomes.description: Plan convergent routes using stereoselective carbon-carbon construction, taught frontier-orbital/pericyclic rules and organo-/metal-catalytic transformations.
Compare mechanistic/spectral evidence for identity and selectivity; optimize bounded synthesis using controls, mass balance and kinetics and justify safety/sustainability tradeoffs.

practice: Defend competing routes and execute or reconstruct a supervised short sequence with purity, identity and waste evidence.

includes: Calibration, titrimetry, gravimetry, chromatography and instrumental quantification

outcomes.description: Apply Beer-Lambert, chromatographic retention/resolution and mass-to-charge separation models to mixtures; diagnose interference and validate spike recovery.
Design sampling, blanks, standards and calibration for titrimetric/gravimetric analyses; estimate concentration, uncertainty, detection limits and matrix effects.

practice: Analyze an unknown by two techniques and reconcile calibration, recovery, detection limits and disagreement.

includes: Biomolecular chemistry, folding, enzymes and central metabolism

outcomes.description: Represent proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids; explain folding, binding, catalysis and membrane assembly using stereochemistry, noncovalent interactions and free energies.
Apply a locally developed steady-state Michaelis-Menten model and inhibition variants; trace carbon, electrons and ATP through respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthetic regulation.

practice: Analyze a metabolic perturbation with molecular structures, stoichiometric balances and enzyme-rate calculations.

includes: Mass-action equilibrium, acid-base chemistry, reaction energy and redox

outcomes.description: Calculate enthalpy, Gibbs-energy changes and cell potentials from data and taught ΔG/Nernst relations; explain activity, standard-state and reversibility limits.
Solve ideal-solution mass-action, mass-balance and charge-balance problems for acids, buffers, complexes and precipitates; test approximation validity.

practice: Predict a titration curve and precipitation sequence and design a concentration-cell comparison.

includes: Rate laws, temperature dependence and mechanism discrimination

outcomes.description: Construct elementary schemes, derive pre-equilibrium and steady-state rate laws and design perturbations distinguishing mechanisms.
Derive zero-, first- and second-order integrated laws and Arrhenius relations; fit transformed or nonlinear models using documented tools and check residuals and uncertainty.

practice: Fit competing kinetic models and propose discriminating concentration, isotope or temperature experiments.

includes: Chemical potentials, nonideal mixtures, phases and response

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic potentials, Maxwell relations, chemical potentials and partial molar quantities; calculate activities/fugacities with specified nonideal models.
Determine reaction and multicomponent phase equilibria, construct phase diagrams and apply phase rule and stability criteria with explicit standard states.

practice: Construct a binary phase diagram and infer nonideality parameters using a supplied solver.

includes: Working electronic calculations, geometry optimization and validation

outcomes.description: Compare energies, geometries and harmonic frequencies with experiment; test basis, conformer, spin and convergence sensitivity and distinguish numerical convergence from model validity.
Implement an orbital secular model and operate documented mean-field/DFT tools using explicitly taught basis, charge, spin, SCF and geometry-convergence settings and assumptions.

practice: Run and audit a conformer/spectrum comparison, including reproducible inputs and intentionally failed convergence cases.

includes: Electrode kinetics, transport, interfacial charge and electrochemical inference

outcomes.description: Fit voltammetry/impedance using documented tools; distinguish kinetic, transport and capacitive effects and assess corrosion, battery or electrocatalytic design tradeoffs.
Derive bounded Butler-Volmer/Tafel, steady diffusion-layer and double-layer circuit models; calculate overpotential, limiting flux and charging with explicit assumptions.

practice: Analyze a cell under potential and frequency perturbations and discriminate mechanisms through residuals and independent controls.

includes: Hartree-Fock, density-functional/correlation models and potential-energy surfaces

outcomes.description: Derive Slater-determinant Hartree-Fock and generalized SCF equations; implement restricted SCF using supplied integrals and explain DFT, perturbative and configuration-interaction correlation approximations.
Calculate geometries, frequencies and reaction paths with documented tools; distinguish basis, correlation, functional, spin and convergence errors against independent evidence.

practice: Implement minimal-basis Hartree-Fock and benchmark a reaction energy across controlled approximation levels.

includes: Organometallic bonding, catalytic cycles and mechanistic evidence

outcomes.description: Derive molecular/surface catalytic rate and selectivity models, teaching site balances and adsorption; distinguish resting states and limiting steps using isotope, spectral, kinetic and poisoning evidence.
Construct orbital/electron-count descriptions and predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion, elimination and ligand-exchange pathways.

practice: Construct competing cycles and design kinetic and spectroscopic tests distinguishing them.

includes: Main-group compounds, crystals, coordination and qualitative ligand fields

outcomes.description: Apply defined crystal-field splitting and spin rules to magnetism; compare ligand substitution, acid-base and redox behavior and state model limits.
Predict main-group bonding, crystal stoichiometry, coordination geometry and isomerism using periodic trends, lattice models and electron counting.

practice: Infer plausible complex structures and spin states from composition, magnetism and reactivity.

includes: Environmental fate, sampling, isotope tracers and dating
excludes: Radiation-handling authorization and spatial transport PDEs

outcomes.description: Construct aqueous/air/soil partition and reaction box balances; analyze acidification, redox, photochemistry and contaminant persistence and justify sampling and remediation decisions.

Calculate isotope ratios, mixing, fractionation and radioactive-decay ages using taught mass-balance/exponential models; design stable-isotope tracing and distinguish reservoir, exchange and contamination effects.

practice: Reconstruct pollutant sources from concentration/isotope data and compare interventions with uncertainty and environmental-justice consequences.

includes: Chemical measurement, preparation, separation, uncertainty and risk

outcomes.description: Compare procedures using exposure, incompatibility, waste and environmental evidence; select controls and justify safer alternatives.
Prepare solutions and perform weighing, volumetric transfer, filtration and recrystallization; calculate uncertainty, recovery and mass balance.

practice: Prepare and recover a benign solute, documenting calibration, uncertainty, waste and comparative risk.

includes: Atoms, periodicity, bonding, molecular geometry and stoichiometry

outcomes.description: Use shell, periodic, Lewis, resonance and electron-pair models to predict bonding, polarity and three-dimensional molecular geometry; identify their limits.
Balance reactions and calculate moles, limiting reagents, yields, concentrations and gas quantities with dimensional checks.

practice: Infer reaction stoichiometry from mass and gas data and reconcile equations with particulate diagrams.

includes: Molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, force fields and free-energy estimation

outcomes.description: Derive free-energy perturbation and umbrella-reweighting estimators; quantify overlap, finite-size, sampling and force-field uncertainty using independent structural/thermodynamic validation.

Implement pair forces, periodic boundaries, neighbor lists, velocity-Verlet and Metropolis moves; derive detailed balance locally and assess ensembles, thermostats, conservation, equilibration and autocorrelation.

practice: Implement a molecular fluid and estimate a free-energy difference with replicate trajectories and overlap/force-field sensitivity studies.

includes: IR, UV-visible, first-order NMR, mass spectra and bounded two-dimensional correlations

outcomes.description: Interpret COSY, HSQC, HMBC and NOE maps using explicitly defined through-bond/space correlation rules, axes and artifacts; propose assignments without claiming spin-dynamics derivations.
Apply taught photon-transition, harmonic-bond, shielding, first-order coupling and ion-fragmentation models; recognize their breakdown.
Combine formulas, isotopes, IR, UV-visible and proton/carbon NMR to distinguish constitutional and stereochemical hypotheses.

practice: Solve blinded one-/two-dimensional spectral unknowns and propose an experiment resolving remaining ambiguity.

includes: Organic structures, stereochemistry, mechanisms and short syntheses

outcomes.description: Use electron-pushing and energy diagrams for substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl reactions, including competing pathways and stereochemical outcomes.
Translate line, Newman, chair and wedge-dash representations; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational, resonance and acid-base stability.
Plan short syntheses using retrosynthetic disconnections, chemoselectivity and protecting groups; identify unsupported selectivity assumptions.

practice: Defend mechanisms and short routes with explicit competing reactions and stereochemical justifications.

includes: Structure-reactivity relations, isotope effects and physical-organic inference

outcomes.description: Combine stereochemical, crossover, trapping, kinetic and thermodynamic evidence to distinguish concerted, stepwise and competing pathways; design falsifying rather than confirmatory experiments.
Derive transition-state/activation parameter relations under stated statistical assumptions; analyze Hammett, Brønsted, solvent and kinetic-isotope correlations and their breakdown.

practice: Infer competing mechanisms from substituent/isotope datasets and propose a minimal discriminating experiment set.

includes: Chain statistics, polymer solutions, phase behavior and rheology

outcomes.description: Derive ideal-chain dimensions and entropic elasticity; analyze excluded-volume scaling and Flory-Huggins mixing/phase diagrams with explicit approximation limits.
Construct Rouse and bounded viscoelastic relaxation models, calculate rheological spectra and infer relaxation distributions from scattering/mechanical data with identifiability checks.

practice: Implement a bead-spring relaxation model and compare chain-size and rheological predictions with independent measurements.

includes: Polymer synthesis, mass distributions and material characterization

outcomes.description: Interpret thermal, mechanical, chromatographic and powder-diffraction data using taught transition, stress-strain and Bragg models; compare polymers, ceramics, glasses and composites and justify lifecycle choices.
Compare step-/chain-growth mechanisms; calculate number-/weight-average molecular masses and relate architecture, crosslinks and tacticity to properties.

practice: Characterize a material from measurements and justify a durability/recyclability recommendation.

includes: Molecular Hamiltonians, orbitals, symmetry and quantum spectra

outcomes.description: Construct Born-Oppenheimer Hamiltonians and orbital secular models; use taught point groups and character tables to form symmetry-adapted orbitals and calculate energies.
Derive rigid-rotor/harmonic vibrational spectra and dipole selection rules; calculate constants and interpret electronic transitions and ligand-field bonding.

practice: Implement a small orbital secular calculation and infer bond length and force constant from spectra.

includes: Adsorption, wetting, micelles and colloidal measurements

outcomes.description: Interpret adsorption isotherms, particle-size scattering, sedimentation and zeta-potential measurements using specified instrument-response models; distinguish aggregation, polydispersity and contamination.
Derive Langmuir adsorption by site balance; apply taught surface-tension, Young-Laplace, contact-angle and micellization models with explicit geometry and assumptions.

practice: Compare two colloidal formulations using adsorption and size data, including dilution controls and model limitations.

includes: Randomized, approximation and online algorithms; advanced optimization guarantees

outcomes.description: Design and prove randomized, approximation and online guarantees using locally derived moment/exponential concentration bounds and adversarial analysis.
Prove LP duality and relaxation bounds; implement a bounded simplex solver and analyze flow integrality, rounding and branch-and-bound certificates and gaps.

practice: Implement exact and approximation allocation algorithms and prove bounds independently of benchmarks.

includes: Neural sequence models, language generation and linguistic evaluation

outcomes.description: Evaluate generation, translation and extraction with held-out and human protocols; test hallucination, contamination, dialect bias and privacy and justify deployment limits.
Derive sequence likelihood and attention-based encoder/decoder objectives; implement a small transformer and compare tokenization, decoding and retrieval-grounding procedures.

practice: Train a small language model and compare decoding/grounding choices on reproducible linguistic and factual error tests.

includes: Search, planning, constraints, logic and discrete probabilistic decisions

outcomes.description: Construct propositional knowledge bases and Bayesian networks; implement elimination inference and finite Markov decision processes using value iteration.
Represent states, actions, constraints and goals; implement A*, adversarial search, constraint propagation and planning with completeness and cost analysis.

practice: Build a grid-world agent and compare search and decision policies under model misspecification.

includes: Digital circuits, instruction sets, memory hierarchy and machine programming

outcomes.description: Construct combinational/sequential Boolean circuits; represent integers and floating-point numbers; trace a simple pipelined processor and cache hierarchy.
Translate C-like programs with pointers, stack frames and heap allocation into assembly; measure locality and diagnose representation and memory errors.

practice: Build a processor in a logic simulator, write assembly and profile cache-sensitive array traversal.

includes: Geometry, projection, rasterization, ray tracing and sampling

outcomes.description: Implement ray intersections, local reflection, texture interpolation and antialiasing; distinguish geometry, lighting and sampling artifacts.
Represent meshes/cameras with homogeneous coordinates; implement rigid/projective transformations, clipping, visibility and barycentric rasterization.

practice: Implement a rasterizer and ray tracer and validate projections and visibility on analytical scenes.

includes: Layered protocols, routing, reliability and sockets

outcomes.description: Implement socket clients/servers and retransmission; interpret packet captures, congestion and protocol failures.
Trace Ethernet, IP, transport, DNS and application exchanges; calculate addressing, delay and throughput; apply taught distance-vector/link-state routing procedures.

practice: Build file transfer over an emulated lossy network and compare measurements with a delay/loss model.

includes: Image formation, filtering, segmentation, motion and multiview reconstruction

outcomes.description: Implement discrete convolution, image derivatives, feature matching, segmentation and linearized optical flow; model sensor noise and use robust fitting to distinguish appearance from motion.

Derive pinhole calibration, epipolar constraints and triangulation in homogeneous coordinates; implement two-view reconstruction and use a documented bundle optimizer with degeneracy and reprojection checks.

practice: Recover a calibrated object's geometry from images and evaluate reconstruction against measured dimensions and adversarial lighting.

includes: Security games, reductions and cryptographic constructions

outcomes.description: Analyze encryption, authenticated encryption, signatures and key exchange using modular arithmetic and stated hardness assumptions; distinguish proof security from randomness and side-channel failures.
Define indistinguishability, pseudorandomness and unforgeability; construct game-based reductions with quantified advantage and computational assumptions.

practice: Write a security reduction and implement a toy construction solely to demonstrate an insecure variant.

includes: Data structures, algorithm design, correctness and complexity

outcomes.description: Implement sorting, traversal, shortest paths and dynamic programming using arrays, trees and adjacency representations.
Prove iterative/recursive correctness, solve runtime recurrences and compare worst-case, average and amortized bounds.
Implement lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, heaps and balanced search-tree operations; compare invariants and costs.

practice: Implement a route planner, prove its invariant and benchmark normal and adversarial inputs.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, storage, transactions and retrieval

outcomes.description: Translate requirements into relational schemas, dependencies and normalization; express queries in relational algebra and SQL.
Implement small index, join and transaction mechanisms; compare query plans and construct an inverted text index with a defined ranking function.

practice: Build a document service, demonstrate transaction anomalies and benchmark indexes and query plans.

includes: Consistency, consensus, fault tolerance and distributed execution

outcomes.description: Specify consistency/failure models, use logical clocks and implement a replicated log with a taught consensus protocol; analyze partitions, recovery and impossibility assumptions.
Construct fault-tolerant distributed data processing with partitioning, retries and checkpointing; analyze communication, skew, consistency and reproducibility beyond single-machine parallelism.

practice: Build a replicated service and distributed job with fault injection, recovery tests and scaling analysis.

includes: Learning theory, kernels, variational models and reinforcement learning

outcomes.description: Derive variational latent-variable objectives and implement a small autoencoder and finite-state reinforcement learner with taught Bellman, policy-gradient and off-policy assumptions.
Derive generalization bounds using concentration and capacity measures; analyze regularization, kernels and optimization/generalization tradeoffs under explicit sampling assumptions.

practice: Reproduce a learning experiment, derive its objective and test a guarantee's assumptions through controlled shift.

includes: Interaction design, accessibility, qualitative inquiry and usability studies

outcomes.description: Elicit needs, construct task models and prototypes and evaluate affordances, cognitive load, recovery and accessibility.
Conduct consent-aware usability studies, code qualitative observations and analyze task outcomes; justify inclusion, convenience and privacy tradeoffs.

practice: Compare prototypes using a prespecified study and accessibility audit, reporting qualitative findings and quantitative uncertainty.

includes: Text processing, linguistic representations, probabilistic sequences and parsing

outcomes.description: Implement hidden-Markov tagging with forward/Viterbi algorithms and chart parsing for probabilistic grammars; evaluate ambiguity, held-out likelihood and task errors.
Implement Unicode-aware tokenization, normalization, finite-state morphology and n-gram models with smoothing; compare corpus, language and domain effects.

practice: Build a tagged-text pipeline and audit errors across dialects and out-of-domain documents.

includes: Parsing, typing, intermediate representations, optimization and code generation

outcomes.description: Construct intermediate representations, implement local dataflow optimization and generate stack-machine or assembly code with runtime storage conventions.
Implement lexical analysis, recursive-descent/table-driven parsing, scope resolution and a static type checker while preserving source-language evaluation rules.

practice: Implement a typed-language compiler and test semantic preservation by differential execution against an interpreter.

includes: Supervised/unsupervised learning, neural representations and evaluation

outcomes.description: Implement linear classifiers, trees, nearest neighbors, k-means, PCA and finite-mixture EM with explicit objectives and update rules.
Design leakage-free evaluation, compare calibration/subgroup errors and justify fairness, interpretation, privacy and deployment-shift decisions.
Derive reverse-mode differentiation and gradient training; implement a small neural network and use documented convolution, attention and sequence models.

practice: Implement baseline and neural models, run ablations and submit reproducible failure analysis and a model card.

includes: Processes, virtual memory, filesystems and concurrency

outcomes.description: Use taught process/thread, lock, condition-variable and atomic APIs; diagnose races, deadlocks and memory-ordering failures.
Implement bounded scheduler, virtual-memory and filesystem components; explain traps, system calls, page tables, caching and crash recovery.

practice: Extend an instructional kernel and stress-test a concurrent server against synchronization invariants.

includes: Shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator-style parallel computation

outcomes.description: Analyze work/span, communication, locality, load balance and floating-point reproducibility; measure scaling and compare CPU and accelerator execution models.
Implement reductions, scans and tiled matrix kernels using taught thread, barrier, atomic and message-passing APIs; identify races and synchronization requirements.

practice: Implement shared-memory and message-passing reductions and a tiled kernel, reporting correctness and scaling bottlenecks.

includes: Imperative programming, functions, collections, files and debugging

outcomes.description: Parse text and tables, validate inputs, transform records and produce documented outputs with error handling.
Trace and write programs using numeric and Boolean expressions, branches, loops, functions, recursion, lists and dictionaries.
Design boundary and example tests, inspect execution state, isolate defects and explain program behavior.

practice: Implement a command-line data cleaner with malformed-input handling, documented functions and automated tests.

includes: Language paradigms, evaluation, binding, interpreters and basic types
excludes: Compiler back ends and soundness metatheory

outcomes.description: Implement an expression-language interpreter using abstract syntax trees and environments; construct and apply simple type-inference/checking rules.
Compare imperative, functional and object-based programs through scope, closures, mutation, evaluation order, recursion, exceptions and data abstraction.

practice: Implement interpreters with two evaluation strategies and explain programs whose behavior differs.

includes: Kinematics, localization, planning and feedback

outcomes.description: Implement configuration-space collision checking, graph/sampling planning and trajectory feedback; test consistency, constraints and human-safety failures.
Construct planar/three-dimensional rigid-transform kinematics and Jacobians; derive Gaussian conditioning and implement Kalman/extended-Kalman localization with sensor models.

practice: Implement simulated localization/navigation and test sensor dropout, obstacle uncertainty and controller failure.

includes: Threat modeling, defenses, authentication and authorized assessment

outcomes.description: Assess injection, authentication, network and memory-boundary failures in isolation; prioritize mitigations and justify disclosure, privacy and usability decisions.
Construct threat models and implement access control, validation, secret handling and secure communication using documented libraries and explicit trust assumptions.

practice: Audit a deliberately vulnerable local service and submit reproduced failures, tested repairs and an authorized disclosure report.

includes: Semantics, type soundness, program logics and model checking

outcomes.description: Specify safety/liveness, derive Hoare proofs and weakest preconditions and implement finite-state model checking with abstraction and state-explosion analysis.
Define small-/big-step semantics and typed lambda-calculus rules; prove substitution, progress and preservation by structural induction.

practice: Prove a language extension sound and verify a locally specified interleaving protocol by invariant and finite-state checker.

includes: Requirements, modular design, testing, delivery and professional judgment

outcomes.description: Deliver a reproducible release and justify reliability, privacy, accessibility, licensing, maintenance and stakeholder-harm tradeoffs.
Translate requirements into interfaces and modules; use version control, code review and unit, integration and acceptance testing.

practice: Deliver a team application with review history, automated tests, release instructions and an evidence-based ethical design decision.

includes: Automata, grammars, Turing machines, reductions and complexity classes

outcomes.description: Construct Turing-machine and problem reductions, prove undecidability and establish NP-completeness while separating computability from resource bounds.
Construct finite/pushdown automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars; prove equivalence and appropriate nonrecognizability claims.

practice: Implement an automaton interpreter and separately prove undecidability and NP-completeness reductions.

includes: Groups, actions, rings, ideals and fields

outcomes.description: Prove and apply subgroup, quotient, isomorphism, group-action and Sylow results to finite groups and symmetries.
Calculate in rings and finite fields; use Euclidean algorithms and ideals; prove factorization and quotient claims for integers and polynomial rings.

practice: Classify small examples and prove when polynomial quotients are fields.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces, energy estimates and numerical convergence theory

outcomes.description: Prove finite-difference stability/convergence and finite-element coercivity, approximation and error estimates; implement adaptive mesh-error assessment on triangular elliptic problems.
Define distributions, weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; derive weak forms and energy estimates and prove representative elliptic existence/uniqueness and parabolic stability.

practice: Prove an energy and discretization error estimate and test predicted rates with manufactured solutions and adaptive refinement.

includes: Commutative algebra and affine/projective algebraic geometry
excludes: Derived geometry and advanced scheme cohomology

outcomes.description: Develop Noetherian rings, localization, integral extensions and prime ideals; prove Hilbert basis and stated Nullstellensatz results and calculate coordinate rings.
Construct affine/projective varieties and morphisms; calculate tangent spaces, singularities and dimensions in explicit examples and relate geometric operations to ring maps.

practice: Analyze a singular curve through equations, local rings and tangent spaces, with proofs connecting each representation.

includes: Chain complexes, homology, cohomology and topological applications

outcomes.description: Construct simplicial/singular chains and induced maps; calculate homology using exact sequences, cellular chains and Mayer-Vietoris; define cochains and cup products.
Prove homotopy invariance and apply degree, Euler characteristic and duality in stated manifold examples to distinguish spaces and establish fixed-point or nonembedding consequences.

practice: Compute invariants of glued cell complexes and prove a topological impossibility not settled by visual inspection.

includes: Single-variable limits, derivatives, integrals and series

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and derivatives, justify local linear approximation and solve rate and optimization problems.
Calculate definite, indefinite and elementary improper integrals using substitution and integration by parts; apply the fundamental theorem.
Determine convergence of standard sequences and series and use Taylor expansions with remainder estimates.

practice: Derive an accumulation model, calculate predictions and bound Taylor approximation error.

includes: Enumeration, graph structure, divisibility and modular arithmetic

outcomes.description: Prove and calculate divisibility, congruence, Chinese-remainder, Euler/Fermat and elementary quadratic-residue results.
Use inclusion-exclusion, generating functions and graph invariants to count structures and prove matching, connectivity and extremal bounds.

practice: Solve a counting problem by two methods and justify an efficient modular computation.

includes: Holomorphic functions, residues and conformal maps

outcomes.description: Evaluate contours with residues, branch choices and arc estimates; construct conformal maps and solve planar potential examples using locally defined harmonic functions and boundary data.
Prove/apply Cauchy-Riemann, Cauchy integral, power-series and maximum-principle results; classify isolated singularities.

practice: Justify a branch-cut integral and map a planar harmonic boundary problem to a solvable domain.

includes: Bayesian models, posterior computation and predictive checks

outcomes.description: Construct conjugate and hierarchical continuous/discrete models; calculate posterior predictions and compare prior sensitivity, identifiability and predictive adequacy.

Implement inverse-CDF/rejection generation, importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs updates; verify finite-state detailed balance and diagnose effective sample size, mixing and weight degeneracy.

practice: Implement a hierarchical posterior analysis and test interval coverage and sampler failure on synthetic data.

includes: Finite differences, introductory finite elements and computational verification

outcomes.description: Implement explicit/implicit finite differences for one-/two-dimensional diffusion, advection and waves; derive truncation and Fourier-mode stability conditions and handle boundary/initial data.

Derive an elliptic weighted-residual form by integration by parts; assemble linear triangular finite elements with quadrature and boundary constraints; verify convergence empirically using manufactured solutions.

practice: Implement finite-difference and triangular-mesh solvers and conduct mesh refinement, conservation and deliberate-instability tests.

includes: Smooth/convex optimization, constrained optimality and solvers

outcomes.description: Establish convexity and derive first/second-order, KKT and dual-bound conditions with explicit constraint qualifications.
Implement gradient, Newton, projected-gradient and basic proximal methods; prove elementary convergence bounds and diagnose scaling and nonconvex failures.

practice: Implement constrained least-squares and sparse-estimation solvers and compare stopping rules with optimality certificates.

includes: Continuous distributions, joint probability, transformations, sampling laws and elementary stochastic processes

outcomes.description: Normalize densities, integrate expectations and derive transformed, conditional and joint distributions; calculate covariance using explicitly taught iterated integrals and elementary Jacobian changes.

Use moment-generating functions, Gaussian/Poisson/exponential models, convolution, laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations; calculate finite-state Markov transitions and Poisson waiting probabilities.

practice: Derive a waiting-time distribution and compare exact and normal-approximate sampling probabilities with a spreadsheet experiment.

includes: ODE solutions, linear systems and phase portraits

outcomes.description: Solve separable/linear first-order and constant-coefficient second-order equations and forced systems using initial conditions, eigenmodes and matrix exponentials.
Construct phase portraits and classify equilibria using locally taught partial derivatives and Jacobian linearization; apply existence/uniqueness conditions in one and two dimensions.

practice: Derive a two-state model and compare analytical solutions and phase portraits with supplied trajectories.

includes: Manifolds, tensors, forms, connections and curvature

outcomes.description: Calculate metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and Riemann/Ricci curvature in Riemannian/Lorentzian examples; relate curvature to invariants.
Construct charts and tangent/cotangent spaces; transform tensors, calculate exterior derivatives/pullbacks and apply manifold Stokes' theorem.

practice: Calculate one curvature invariant in two charts and derive surface and Lorentzian geodesics.

includes: Nonlinear dynamics, time integration, feedback and deterministic observers

outcomes.description: Construct state-space and transfer-function models, test controllability/observability and design pole-placement feedback and Luenberger observers with robustness checks.
Analyze Jacobian/Lyapunov stability and elementary bifurcations; implement Euler and Runge-Kutta integration with step-size and stability checks.

practice: Implement a controlled two-state plant and demonstrate failure from delay, model error and excessive integration steps.

includes: Banach/Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded operators and spectra

outcomes.description: Prove completeness of sequence/function spaces; apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results; distinguish weak and norm convergence using locally developed dual topologies.
Analyze bounded/compact operators, adjoints and spectra; prove Hilbert projection and compact self-adjoint spectral results and apply variational solvability arguments.

practice: Prove stability and solvability of a variational problem and construct a failure when coercivity is lost.

includes: Modules, extensions, Galois theory and representations

outcomes.description: Prove/apply Galois correspondence to polynomial solvability and construct complex finite-group representations and character decompositions.
Analyze PID modules, exact sequences and tensor products; relate module structure to canonical forms and calculate field extensions.

practice: Determine a polynomial's Galois group and decompose a finite-group action with full justification.

includes: Decision/likelihood theory, asymptotics and theoretical Bayesian computation

outcomes.description: Prove invariant-distribution and stated ergodic results for importance/MCMC estimators; analyze posterior concentration and Monte Carlo uncertainty under explicit regularity and mixing conditions.
Analyze sufficiency, information, optimal tests and estimator risk; derive regular likelihood consistency/asymptotic normality and explain boundary and misspecification failures.

practice: Derive a limiting law and test coverage and Monte Carlo error where regularity holds and fails.

includes: Vector spaces, matrices, eigenstructure, projections and least squares

outcomes.description: Construct projections, least-squares solutions and singular-value decompositions; diagnose rank deficiency.
Solve linear systems by elimination and represent maps through bases, rank, null spaces, determinants and coordinate changes.
Compute eigenstructure and use real/complex inner products, orthogonal/unitary bases and symmetric/Hermitian diagonalization.

practice: Recover an unknown vector from noisy measurements and compare exact, least-squares and rank-truncated solutions.

includes: Linear programming, dual certificates, network models and integer optimization

outcomes.description: Formulate flow, matching, scheduling and integer models; apply taught augmenting-path and branch-and-bound procedures manually and with documented solvers, reporting relaxation bounds and gaps.
Translate constraints into matrix linear programs; perform simplex pivots, interpret primal/dual certificates and sensitivity, and diagnose infeasibility or unboundedness.

practice: Solve a resource-allocation model by hand and with a solver, then compare its integer and relaxed solutions.

includes: First-order syntax/semantics, completeness, computability and incompleteness

outcomes.description: Define effective procedures through register machines and encodings; prove undecidability by diagonalization and explain/prove a stated incompleteness theorem with explicit representability hypotheses.
Construct first-order structures and derivations; prove soundness and a countable-language completeness theorem and apply compactness to distinguish theories and models.

practice: Build contrasting models and write a diagonalization proof, identifying syntactic versus semantic claims.

includes: Measure, Lebesgue integration and probabilistic limits

outcomes.description: Construct measures, measurable functions and Lebesgue integrals; prove/apply convergence, product-integration and Radon-Nikodym results with explicit hypotheses.
Develop conditional expectation and characteristic functions; prove laws of large numbers and a central limit theorem and analyze elementary martingales and modes of stochastic convergence.

practice: Write measure-theoretic proofs and counterexamples comparing almost-sure, probability and distributional convergence.

includes: Multivariable differentiation, curves, surfaces and vector calculus

outcomes.description: Parametrize curves and surfaces; calculate tangents, normals, arc length, area and elementary curvature.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, constrained extrema and multiple integrals with two-/three-dimensional coordinate changes.
Calculate line/surface integrals, divergence, curl and Laplacians in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates; apply Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems.

practice: Represent a three-dimensional field in two coordinate systems and verify an integral theorem on a curved boundary.

includes: Floating-point error, roots, interpolation, quadrature and matrix algorithms

outcomes.description: Implement pivoted elimination and QR least squares, use an SVD library transparently and diagnose ill-conditioning using residuals and perturbations.
Implement bisection, Newton iteration, interpolation and composite quadrature; derive elementary error estimates and distinguish conditioning, truncation and roundoff.

practice: Implement a tested numerical library and exhibit a small-residual, large-solution-error example.

includes: Finite probability, descriptive statistics and sampling

outcomes.description: Summarize data graphically and numerically; distinguish sampling and measurement bias; interpret sampling variation using supplied normal models or spreadsheet simulation.
Construct finite sample spaces; apply conditional probability and Bayes' rule; calculate expectations and variances of discrete models.

practice: Analyze diagnostic-test base rates and conduct a spreadsheet sampling experiment across sample sizes.

includes: Logic, proof, sets, relations, graphs, counting and recurrences

outcomes.description: Construct sets, functions, relations, finite graphs and trees; count arrangements and solve elementary recurrences.
Translate quantified statements and prove or refute claims using direct proof, contradiction, contraposition and ordinary or structural induction.

practice: Write proofs of an induction claim and graph invariant and construct a counterexample to a plausible false statement.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, coordinates, vectors and complex numbers

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, powers, logarithms and units; solve equations and interpret linear, exponential and trigonometric functions in tables and graphs.
Use Cartesian and polar coordinates, similarity, areas and volumes; calculate with two- and three-dimensional vectors, dot/cross products and rectangular/polar complex numbers.

practice: Construct a unit-consistent measurement model and solve a spatial problem using both diagrams and algebra.

includes: Completeness, metric limits, continuity and function convergence

outcomes.description: Distinguish pointwise/uniform convergence and prove or refute interchange of limits, derivatives, sums and integrals under explicit hypotheses.
Use completeness, compactness and epsilon-delta arguments to prove sequence, continuity, differentiation and Riemann-integration results on intervals and metric spaces.

practice: Write proofs and counterexamples identifying exactly where completeness, compactness or uniformity is required.

includes: Intervals, tests, simple regression, randomization and study design

outcomes.description: Calculate confidence intervals and one-/two-sample tests using normal, t, binomial or randomization procedures; distinguish effect size, uncertainty and multiplicity.
Fit simple linear regression using stated formulas or a tool, check residuals and identify confounding, pseudoreplication, randomization and blocking needs.

practice: Analyze randomized and observational datasets, including a tool-based bootstrap, residual plots and limits-of-inference statement.

includes: Multivariate regression, GLMs, likelihood and validation

outcomes.description: Implement bootstrap, permutation, cross-validation and false-discovery control; diagnose leakage, misspecification, confounding and unstable coefficients.
Construct Gaussian linear, logistic and Poisson models in matrix form; derive likelihoods/gradients, fit with documented optimizers and interpret interactions, regularization and uncertainty.

practice: Build a reproducible regression analysis with implemented resampling and a predictive-versus-causal interpretation defense.

includes: Markov processes, martingales, Brownian motion and Ito calculus

outcomes.description: Derive discrete/continuous-time Markov transition and generator equations; apply stopping and martingale arguments under explicit integrability conditions.
Construct Brownian increments, define Ito integration, derive Ito's formula and solve elementary SDEs; implement Euler-Maruyama and assess strong/weak error and stopping bias.

practice: Prove a stopping-time result and implement an SDE experiment with coupled step-refinement tests.

includes: Topological spaces, compactness, connectedness, quotients and fundamental groups

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary fundamental groups using taught homotopy, covering-space and van Kampen methods; distinguish spaces and identify limits of pictures.
Construct subspace, product and quotient topologies; prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties.

practice: Analyze glued polygons, prove a quotient property and calculate a fundamental group.

includes: Fourier/Laplace methods, eigenfunctions and classical boundary problems

outcomes.description: Solve heat, wave and Laplace problems on intervals, rectangles, cylinders and spheres using separation, locally developed Sturm-Liouville theory and Bessel/Legendre functions.
Calculate Fourier series, Fourier/Laplace transforms and convolutions; apply orthogonality and stated convergence conditions to forced linear problems.

practice: Derive fields in two geometries and check boundary conditions and truncated-expansion convergence.

includes: Variational calculus, Lagrangian/Hamiltonian mechanics and constraints

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations; analyze rigid bodies, small oscillations and central-force phase space.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations, use generalized coordinates/constraints and connect symmetries to conservation through a taught Noether argument.

practice: Derive a constrained multibody system in two coordinate choices and verify identical trajectories and conserved quantities.

includes: Observational astronomy, stars, galaxies and empirical cosmology

outcomes.description: Use sky coordinates, parallax, magnitudes, flux, spectral lines, Doppler shifts and light curves to infer distance, temperature, mass, radius and orbits with degeneracy checks.
Apply taught blackbody laws, hydrostatic scaling, nuclear-energy bookkeeping and Hubble relations to stellar evolution, galaxies and dark-component evidence.

practice: Infer a stellar/planetary system from archival light curves and spectra, reporting competing parameter explanations.

includes: Atomic transitions, coherent driving, lasers and quantum-optical measurements

outcomes.description: Derive driven two-level and optical-Bloch equations with stated relaxation models; calculate Rabi oscillations, line shapes, selection rules and laser gain/threshold.
Construct coherent/Fock-state and photon-correlation predictions; analyze interferometric, lifetime and antibunching measurements with detector response and classical alternative tests.

practice: Fit coherent-drive and photon-counting data and justify whether nonclassical claims survive background and detector corrections.

includes: DC/phasor networks, bounded RC response, sensors and electronics

outcomes.description: Apply Kirchhoff laws, equivalent circuits and complex impedances; use a taught exponential RC model with explicit initial conditions and limitations.
Design readouts using idealized diode, transistor-switch and op-amp models; select gain, grounding, filtering and sampling and diagnose loading, clipping and aliasing.

practice: Validate an amplifier/filter using a circuit simulator and acquire calibrated signals with a meter and oscilloscope.

includes: Crystals, bands, phonons, transport, magnetism and soft matter

outcomes.description: Calculate phonons, heat capacities and Drude transport; analyze bounded spin, elastic and polymer-chain models and interpret magnetic, liquid-crystalline and superconducting evidence.
Construct reciprocal lattices/zones, derive one-dimensional nearly-free and tight-binding bands and apply taught Fermi occupation/density-of-states models to metals and semiconductors.

practice: Infer material parameters from diffraction, heat-capacity and conductivity data and identify microscopic-model failures.

includes: Deformation, stress, elasticity, viscoelasticity and constitutive validation

outcomes.description: Derive material/spatial deformation maps, strain and stress transformations and balance laws; construct frame-indifferent elastic/viscoelastic laws consistent with energy and dissipation.
Derive variational elasticity and coupled continuum models, implement bounded finite-element examples and discriminate constitutive laws using loading-history data and mesh/parameter sensitivity.

practice: Fit elastic/viscoelastic constitutive alternatives and validate a deformation computation against independent loading histories.

includes: Static fields, material response, Maxwell equations and plane waves

outcomes.description: Use integral/differential Maxwell equations to derive induction, field energy and plane waves; calculate Lorentz-force motion and energy transfer.
Calculate fields/potentials from continuous charge and current; apply symmetry, Gauss/Ampere laws and conductor/dielectric boundary conditions in three dimensions.

practice: Solve contrasting electrostatic configurations and derive a plane-wave energy balance.

includes: Instrument integration, signal extraction and inverse measurement

outcomes.description: Integrate sensors, optics, electronics and acquisition; implement locally taught discrete Fourier analysis, lock-in demodulation and noise spectra with calibration/sampling checks.
Estimate parameters using weighted least squares and a locally derived Jacobian covariance approximation; compare systematic-error models and justify safety, reproducibility and impact decisions.

practice: Complete an optical/electromechanical measurement with a noise budget, independent calibration and reproducible uncertainty analysis.

includes: Viscous incompressible flow, vorticity, boundary layers and computation

outcomes.description: Derive continuity and Newtonian Navier-Stokes equations in Cartesian/tensor-component form; nondimensionalize, derive vorticity balances and solve Couette, Poiseuille, creeping and boundary-layer examples.

Implement a bounded two-dimensional incompressible projection solver with pressure boundary conditions; validate divergence, conservation, grid error and flow-regime assumptions against benchmark and laboratory data.

practice: Solve a viscous-flow benchmark and compare a two-dimensional computation with measured velocity or pressure data.

includes: Hydrostatics, control-volume flow, viscosity and fluid measurement

outcomes.description: Calculate Reynolds number and drag/pressure-loss predictions with stated correlations; measure flow rate, viscosity and pressure drop and distinguish laminar, entrance and turbulent regimes.
Apply hydrostatics and control-volume mass, momentum and energy balances; derive Bernoulli and plane/pipe laminar flow from pressure and Newtonian shear using one-dimensional integration.

practice: Measure pressure drop versus flow in a safe liquid circuit and test viscosity and regime assumptions.

includes: Einstein equations, relativistic matter, Schwarzschild geometry and gravitational waves

outcomes.description: Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, precession, deflection and horizon properties; derive linearized gravitational waves and detector strain.
Construct particle/perfect-fluid stress-energy tensors, derive geodesics variationally and apply Einstein equations and covariant conservation to symmetric metrics.

practice: Derive two observable relativistic corrections and analyze curvature and causal behavior near a horizon.

includes: Green functions, multipoles, waveguides, radiation and covariance

outcomes.description: Construct Green functions and multipoles, solve cylindrical/spherical boundaries and derive guided-wave and dielectric-interface modes.
Derive retarded potentials and dipole radiation, calculate angular power and express Maxwell equations/transformations in locally taught covariant tensor notation.

practice: Derive a waveguide mode and radiating-source field, checking boundaries, gauge consistency and energy.

includes: Quantum approximation, angular momentum, scattering and composite states

outcomes.description: Derive variational, WKB, degenerate and time-dependent perturbation methods; combine angular momenta and solve central potentials using taught Frobenius methods.
Calculate Born/partial-wave scattering; construct bosonic/fermionic states and density matrices; analyze reduced states, entanglement and measurement statistics.

practice: Compare variational and numerical bound states and calculate scattering with approximation-validity checks.

includes: Kinetic plasma theory, damping, MHD and magnetized transport

outcomes.description: Derive Vlasov and moment equations from phase-space transport; calculate dielectric response and Landau damping with contour prescriptions and implement a bounded one-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell scheme.
Derive MHD closure and Alfvén/magnetosonic modes, analyze stated stability and collisional transport models and validate conservation, resolution and closure limits.

practice: Implement particle deposition, field solution and leapfrog pushing; compare damping with kinetic and fluid predictions.

includes: Second quantization, Green functions, response and collective order

outcomes.description: Derive linear-response and spectral observables and representative BCS or spin-wave theories; compare quasiparticle, mean-field and correlation predictions against scattering/transport evidence.
Construct second-quantized lattice/continuum Hamiltonians; derive noninteracting Green functions, Wick contractions and bounded perturbative/Hartree-Fock approximations.

practice: Calculate a spectral or response function and test a collective-order approximation against limiting cases and published-style data.

includes: Particle and rigid-body mechanics, conservation and orbits

outcomes.description: Apply energy, momentum and angular-momentum conservation to collisions, central forces and Kepler orbits; infer force parameters from trajectories.
Formulate vector Newton equations in Cartesian and plane-polar coordinates; calculate integrable trajectories and rotational motion using torque and moment of inertia.

practice: Derive and test an orbital or rotational model, estimating parameters from positions or periods.

includes: Special relativity and empirical quantum origins
excludes: General relativity and Schrödinger solution methods

outcomes.description: Analyze photoelectric, Compton, atomic-spectrum and matter-wave evidence with photon/de Broglie relations and identify semiclassical limitations.
Calculate Lorentz transformations, intervals, four-momentum conservation and collision thresholds using a defined Minkowski metric.

practice: Reconstruct a relativistic collision and infer constants from photoelectric and spectral data.

includes: Nuclear models, decay, reactions and particle detector evidence

outcomes.description: Calculate binding, decay chains, tunneling and reaction Q-values using liquid-drop, shell and barrier models; distinguish fission, fusion and decay.
Apply conservation, invariant mass and cross-section definitions to reactions; interpret tracking, calorimetry and counts with taught efficiency, Poisson and background models.

practice: Reconstruct a resonance from simulated events and test efficiency and background explanations.

includes: Ray optics, scalar interference, diffraction and optical measurement

outcomes.description: Apply taught sinusoidal phase addition, slit/grating/aperture and polarization-intensity models; infer wavelength or size and identify resolution and model limits.
Construct ray diagrams and calculate imaging, magnification, reflection, refraction and paraxial lens-system performance.

practice: Measure focal length or wavelength, quantifying alignment and measurement uncertainty.

includes: Oscillators, normal modes, mechanical waves, acoustics and dispersion

outcomes.description: Derive and solve damped, driven and coupled oscillator equations; calculate resonance, phase and normal modes.
Derive one-dimensional string/acoustic wave equations from balances; verify traveling/standing solutions and calculate reflection, impedance, dispersion and energy flux.

practice: Measure resonances and infer damping and wave speed from amplitude/phase data.

includes: Forces, pressure, elementary motion, energy and measurement

outcomes.description: Measure length, time, mass and motion; estimate resolution and repeatability, propagate simple independent uncertainties and compare measurements with predictions.
Construct free-body diagrams and use algebraic force, pressure, constant-acceleration, momentum and energy models in one and two dimensions.

practice: Measure rolling-object motion, calibrate the method and determine whether discrepancies exceed measurement uncertainty.

includes: Plasma scales, particle motion, screening and cold-fluid waves

outcomes.description: Calculate gyration and guiding-center drifts; derive Debye screening using a taught Boltzmann-density closure and identify quasineutrality, collision and magnetization regimes.

Derive cold-fluid continuity/momentum closures and linear plasma oscillation and magnetized-wave dispersion; infer density and temperature from supplied probe/microwave models with sheath and calibration limitations.

practice: Analyze archived probe and wave data and distinguish screening, collisional and collective interpretations.

includes: Relativistic fields, quantization, propagators and perturbative renormalization
excludes: Quantum gravity and exhaustive Standard Model phenomenology

outcomes.description: Derive scalar, Dirac and electromagnetic field equations from actions; construct mode expansions, commutation/anticommutation relations and propagators using canonical and discretized Gaussian path-integral methods.

Derive Wick expansion and Feynman rules, calculate tree-level amplitudes and a scalar one-loop correction, and apply explicit regularization/renormalization conditions while checking symmetries and dimensions.

practice: Derive a tree-level cross section and renormalized scalar one-loop observable, separating regulator dependence from physical parameters.

includes: Quantum states, operators, one-dimensional potentials, spin and atomic states

outcomes.description: Solve wells, barriers and harmonic oscillators; calculate spin measurements, commutators and first-order perturbations; interpret supplied hydrogen eigenfunctions and three-dimensional quantum numbers.
Normalize wavefunctions, calculate probability and expectation integrals, use bra-ket/Hermitian-operator notation and evolve finite-dimensional states unitarily.

practice: Calculate barrier transmission and sequential spin probabilities, checking normalization and limiting cases.

includes: Grand ensembles, quantum gases and phase transitions

outcomes.description: Derive mean-field/Landau ordering models, analyze correlations and critical scaling and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance and finite-size checks.
Derive Bose/Fermi occupations from state counting; calculate blackbody, degenerate-gas and condensation observables and thermodynamic limits.

practice: Compare a sampled spin transition with mean-field predictions and calculate quantum-gas thermodynamics with numerical error control.

includes: Classical ensembles, fluctuations and microscopic transport models

outcomes.description: Construct microcanonical/canonical ensembles, derive Boltzmann weights and partition relations and calculate gas, oscillator and discrete-spin thermodynamics.
Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response; derive Maxwell velocity distributions and random-walk/kinetic estimates of diffusion and transport.

practice: Derive a model's thermodynamics and compare fluctuation or diffusion measurements with microscopic assumptions.

includes: Stellar structure, radiative transfer, compact objects and quantitative cosmology

outcomes.description: Apply stated Friedmann equations and equations of state to expansion, distances and horizons; fit bounded cosmologies and assess degeneracy without claiming an Einstein-equation derivation.
Derive/integrate spherical stellar mass, pressure, luminosity and temperature equations with stated opacity/nuclear rates; solve one-dimensional radiative transfer and analyze degenerate support.

practice: Implement stellar shooting and compare expansion-distance models with archival data using a supplied least-squares tool.

includes: Thermal laws, equations of state, entropy and engines

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy changes and engine/refrigerator performance through reversible reference paths; diagnose irreversibility and distinguish state and path quantities.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes for gases, calorimetry, phase changes and elementary conduction using stated constitutive laws.

practice: Reconstruct an engine cycle from pressure-volume data and audit energy and entropy balances.
